What the numbers say

In this revision 47 option-selling candidates across 14 underlyings passed the report's filters, all of them short puts. Expiries run from 2 to 67 days out with a median of 18 days; 11 of the 47 expire within seven days and 5 are more than 21 days out.

The highest composite score is 59.8 for the UNH 340 put expiring 2026-10-16 (4 days): premium $1.38, strike 10.1% below the share price, model probability of expiring out of the money 88.5%. Its displayed annualized yield of 37.0% multiplies a 4-day premium out to a full year, which is why the score discounts yields from contracts shorter than 30 days.

Implied volatility among the listed contracts is highest for MRVL (60.8%), ISRG (58.8%), UNH (55.6%) and lowest for COST (19.0%). High implied volatility is what makes a premium large; it is the market's price for a wide expected range, so the richest premiums sit on the names the market expects to move most.

Of the 27 underlyings with a quote, 14 were up and 13 down when the report was generated; the median move was +0.01%. Rising share prices move existing short puts further out of the money and shrink the premium available on new ones.

Backtest reference

The report carries a fixed reference backtest covering 2026-03-26 to 2026-04-22: 2,149 simulated option-selling trades with a 83.3% win rate and a profit factor of 0.70. A profit factor below 1 means total losses exceeded total gains even though most trades won. That is the characteristic risk of selling premium: many small wins and a few large losses. The window is short and does not include the session on this page; it is a description of that period, not an estimate of future results.
